content: Labored breathing, also referred to as labored respiration, is an abnormal respiratory pattern that is characterized by visible signs of increased effort required to breathe. This includes the engagement of accessory muscles of respiration, the presence of stridor (a high-pitched wheezing sound), grunting, or nasal flaring. It is important to differentiate labored breathing from the sensation of shortness of breath or dyspnea. While labored breathing is a physical manifestation of respiratory difficulty, shortness of breath or dyspnea refers to the subjective experience or sensation of respiratory distress.
